title: Base Role Definition
description: Schema for AI agent role definitions. Each role is a composable building block that contributes one dimension of behavior (lifecycle stage, architectural layer, language expertise, or quality concern).

name.description: Unique identifier for this role. Lowercase with hyphens.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this role does and when to use it.

version.description: Semantic version. Bump major for breaking responsibility changes, minor for new guidelines, patch for wording fixes.

type.description: Role category. Determines how this role composes with others: lifecycle (what work), layer (where in the stack), language (what ecosystem), mixin (crosscutting concern), system (baseline/router infrastructure).

responsibilities.description: What this role actively does. Each item should be a concrete, actionable statement.

non_responsibilities.description: Explicit boundaries. What this role does NOT do. Used for conflict detection: an item cannot appear in both responsibilities and non_responsibilities of a composed role.

guidelines.description: Actionable rules, preferences, and principles. Should be specific enough to influence decisions, not vague platitudes.

name.description: Tool name as typically invoked (e.g., 'pytest', 'dotnet format').

purpose.description: What this role uses the tool for (e.g., 'unit testing', 'code formatting').

when.description: Selection guidance — when to reach for this tool vs alternatives (e.g., 'primary linter; supersedes flake8 and isort'). Helps simpler models choose the right tool.

tools.description: Tools this role should prefer. The role says when/why to use the tool; it does not re-document how the tool works.

input.description: What the role receives (code snippet, question, artifact).

output.description: What the role produces (review comment, code, design decision).

examples.description: Concrete examples of the role in action. Demonstrates expected behavior for ambiguous situations.

tone.description: Communication style. Typically set by lifecycle roles; layer, language, and mixin roles usually omit this to inherit from the lifecycle role.

output_format.description: How to structure the output. Like tone, typically set by lifecycle roles.

context.description: Additional structured context: framework preferences, conventions, environment details. Free-form key-value pairs.

check.description: What to verify (e.g., 'Code passes linting', 'Business logic separated from handlers').

command.description: Shell command to run for automated verification. Omit for checks that require AI self-assessment.

verification.description: Concrete checks to verify role compliance. Checks with a command are run automatically; checks without a command are self-assessed by the AI.

min_tier.description: Minimum model capability tier. 'fast' = small/cheap models (Haiku-class), 'standard' = mid-range (Sonnet-class), 'advanced' = frontier (Opus-class).

reasoning.description: Recommended reasoning depth. 'none' = straightforward tasks, 'standard' = analysis and tradeoffs, 'extended' = deep multi-step reasoning.

model_requirements.description: Minimum model requirements for this role to function well. The composer aggregates across all roles (taking the max) and adds a composition complexity bonus. Default is fast/none.
